neighbours.label: in narrative prose, the word just before a verb of something arising or developing over time ('soon arose', 'gradually arose', 'grew to be', 'decay was doing its work')
fire: The two brothers were raised together, but jealousy soon arose between them.
Over the long winter a bitter quarrel gradually arose among the settlers.
The orphan girl grew to be the fairest maiden in the whole valley.
As the years passed, a deep friendship slowly developed between the old men.
Within a month a rumour began to spread through the village.
In time a strange coldness grew up between the king and his son.
From these small disputes a lasting hatred eventually sprang up.
Little by little the rust was eating away at the iron gate.
quiet: The two brothers were raised together and lived in the same house.
Over the long winter the settlers stayed inside their wooden cabins.
The orphan girl lived with her aunt in a cottage in the valley.
As the years passed, the old men sat each evening by the fire.
Within a month the village held its yearly harvest fair.
In those days the king and his son lived in the northern castle.
Those small disputes were settled by the elders in the square.
The iron gate stood at the end of the long gravel path.

notes: Card flags broad (1.2% of tokens reach 0.1 of max); top examples are archaic narrative where a feud or quality emerges. Near misses keep the narrative style but describe static states.
